plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock exit points. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it neither costs you when you'd lose anyway (bidding higher just risks overpaying) nor forgoes profitable wins (bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities). Since my value is $31, I will bid exactly that amount to maximize expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the prize is worth if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid equals my true value of $22.

This mechanism functions as a second-price auction: I pay the second-highest bid if I win, and my exit point is determined by my own sealed bid. Since payment depends on others' bids, not my own, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($40). Bidding higher risks overpaying above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.
